title: Shared compression library: clock fallback invalidated the NUMA run
headline: NUMA functional checks passed; clocksource fallback made the run invalid.

sections.title: Functional success and run validity are separate requirements
sections.lead: R4 tested the unchanged library with an explicit two-socket NUMA topology. Its fresh baseline passed. The NUMA functional checks passed, while a frozen clock-validity requirement rejected the run and closed this contract.

blocks.text: The NUMA result is warning-free. Library placement, CPU hotplug and memory-accounting subcases passed. Its saved integration_pass is true and run_valid is false; both fields remain intact.
R4 consumed 2 probe guests and no new builds. Through this closeout, the four contracts consumed 10 guests and 4 builds. No candidate debug case, later matrix row, calibration or timing ran in R4.

sections.title: 1. Whole system: restore the application page
sections.lead: An application needs its full page in physical RAM. Stored contents may be compressed inside RAM or reside on a backing device. Compression trades CPU work for less storage traffic.

blocks.takeaway: The changed engine serves compressed contents inside RAM
blocks.note: Schematic path, with no illustrative size or timing used as a measurement.

blocks.text: The candidate changes the compressed-storage implementation. The existing frontend still decides admission, accounting and writeback. No new RAM-to-disk migration policy is implemented here.

sections.title: 2. Subsystem: policy keeps the object identity
sections.lead: ZSwap retains the entry index, memory-group charge, ordering and lifetime pins. A shared page library owns per-CPU codec contexts, scratch buffers and compressed-object storage.

blocks.takeaway: Data moves through the engine; policy stays with the frontend

blocks.text: High-confidence source review supports this unchanged ownership boundary. NUMA functional observations now cover placement, hotplug and accounting without kernel warnings. The separate clock-validity failure still prevents a valid complete matrix.

sections.title: 3. Concrete observation: the boot clock changed before hotplug
sections.lead: The retained kernel log marks TSC unstable, then records selection of HPET. The CPU hotplug subcase begins later. This ordering separates the recorded boot event from later test execution.

blocks.takeaway: Recorded ordering: boot clock events precede CPU offline
Functional gates and validity both control coverage

blocks.text: The baseline is valid and functionally passed. The NUMA run exited normally with successful subcase resets, but clocksource_fallback makes it invalid. These observations do not complete candidate correctness or establish a performance result.

sections.title: Review the clock environment before another contract
sections.lead: The closed R4 record preserves the invalid run. A separately reviewed environment contract must retain strict validity checks and collect fresh required correctness evidence before any timing comparison.

blocks.takeaway: A reviewed environment still needs fresh valid coverage

blocks.text: Confidence is high in the recorded outcomes and boot-event order. Cause analysis and any proposed environment change are separate evidence. Their execution outcome is unmeasured here; original costs and the earlier deadline remain binding.

patches.takeaway: Same K1: the API keeps publication, accounting and handle lifetime with its caller
Same K1: the library compresses and allocates before returning a usable handle
Same K1: frontend pool creation delegates the engine and preserves its reference lifetime

patches_lead: The exact K1 source remains unchanged across all four infrastructure contracts. These pinned excerpts explain the shared-library hypothesis; R4 adds functional observations, not a new kernel change.
